residual_observed_on_unpatched_vps.detail: Optimistic dot y stayed at 469.77 for samples 40-240ms. Confirmed dot appeared at 280ms at y=470.94 -> a single 1.17px discontinuous vertical step exactly at the swap. The chart's price scale did NOT rescale in that window (live-price-line y drifted continuously 473.27 -> 474.07 in the same window). Root cause: unpatched VPS ignores clientTickT and stamps entry_price at engine.price(symbol) after the tick advanced by one increment (entry_price=1.09381 while the optimistic price = the last tick the browser rendered, ~1.09380). This is exactly what the user's patch fixes; once /app/backend/deploy/patch_trade_price.sh is executed on the VPS, entry_price will equal engine.price_at(clientTickT) and this 1.17px residual disappears.
residual_observed_on_unpatched_vps.expected_after_patch: delta between optimistic and confirmed dot y at the swap -> 0 (both come from the same tick's price).

critical_code_review_comments: Engine.price_at correctly handles empty ticks deque (returns current price), invalid ts (TypeError/ValueError -> current price), and future ts (>= last tick t -> current price). The reversed-linear scan is O(n) but fine because ticks is a bounded deque(maxlen=400000) and the loop breaks on the first t<=ts.

trade_routes.place_trade_core window (wall-3.0 <= ts <= wall+0.5) is deliberately asymmetric to accept mild client-clock skew forward (0.5s) and network delay backward (3s). Combined with engine tick_all cadence of 0.25s this yields a comfortable margin without ever accepting a truly stale tick.

ws_routes._settle_one selects orders via `Order.expiry_at <= now` and then uses engine.price_at(order.symbol, order.expiry_at.timestamp()) so even if the loop runs 100-900ms late, the exit price is the tick at (or immediately before) the expiry instant -> the win/loss verdict cannot flip because of post-expiry ticks. Correct.
settle_loop asyncio.sleep(0.1) delivers <=100ms latency between expiry and s_orders/close in the common case, which matches the 'result card appears immediately' UX goal.

DemoTrade.jsx s_orders/open handler now strips the optimistic placeholder in the SAME setOpenTrades transition -- fully eliminates the transient duplicate observed in earlier iterations. Verified live: 0 samples with >1 dot for the trade during the 1.6s swap window.

Nit: patch_trade_price.sh uses `systemctl restart bfg-backend || service bfg-backend restart || true`. The `|| true` masks a real failure to restart. Consider dropping the `|| true` after the fallback so the operator sees a non-zero exit if BOTH restart methods fail.

rca of the issue: Two root causes, both server-side, both addressed by /app/backend/deploy/patch_trade_price.sh: (1) place_trade previously stamped entry_price at engine.price(symbol), which is the tick AFTER the one the browser last rendered because engine.tick_all runs every 250ms while socket delivery + click handling adds latency -> a 1-tick drift -> the on-chart entry dot moved by ~one price digit's worth of pixels (~1-2px) at the optimistic->confirmed swap. Fix: the frontend now sends clientTickT (timestamp of the tick it saw), and the server reads engine.price_at(sym, ts) so the confirmed entry_price is identical to the optimistic one. (2) settle_loop used engine.price(symbol) (=current price) and slept 1s, so if the loop ran 300-1000ms after expiry and adverse ticks arrived in that window, a winning trade could settle as a loss. Fix: engine.price_at(sym, expiry_at.timestamp()) reads the tick at the expiry instant regardless of when the settle loop runs, and the sleep is dropped to 100ms so the client sees the result within ~100ms of expiry. Verified statically + unit-tested; end-to-end verification is on the user post-patch.
